registry: The registry entry holds the facts disclosures draw on: purpose, provider, version, jurisdictions, and whether the system talks to people, generates content or decides about them.
trigger: An incident, a personal data breach, a material change, a deprecation or a retirement emits a trigger that starts a clock.
matrix: The duty matrix maps registry facts and triggers to audiences, surfaces, templates and clocks, per jurisdiction.
templates: Templates per audience and language live in version control; a template change is a reviewed diff, and holding statements exist in skeleton.
approve: One owner approves what goes out, so the organisation speaks with one voice.
proactive: Proactive disclosures: the AI-interaction notice, content labels, the transparency page and system card, and notices to workers and affected people.
reactive: Triggered notifications to the provider, authorities, affected people, business customers and the public, each on its clock.
record: Each notice sent records its audience, trigger, template version, approver, channel and timestamp.
